title: Structure-based strategy reveals a novel ligand binding site in Staphylococcus aureus catabolite control protein A: implications for transcriptional regulation and drug design
authors: André Borges Farias; Maria Carolina Sisco; Maiana de Oliveira Cerqueira Costa; Ernesto Perez-Rueda; MARISA FABIANA NICOLÁS
one_liner_zh: 该文通过结构比对策略预测金黄色葡萄球菌转录因子CcpA的新配体结合位点，并结合分子动力学与对接研究其稳定性，虽非直接研究TF-DNA互作，但聚焦转录因子结构功能与药物设计，方法可迁移至TF-DNA结合位点预测。
abstract: Staphylococcus aureus is a major human pathogen responsible for a broad spectrum of infections and is recognized by the World Health Organization as a high-priority antimicrobial-resistant organism. The global transcription factor (TF) catabolite control protein A (CcpA), a central regulator of metabolism and virulence, represents a promising drug target. However, efforts to design inhibitors are hindered by their closed crystallographic conformation and the absence of well-defined ligand-binding cavities. Here, we present a structure-guided alignment strategy to identify potential ligand-binding sites in CcpA from S. aureus (Sa-CcpA), using a curated set of co-crystallized TFs as structural templates. This methodology identified a putative ligand-binding site in Sa-CcpA that was not predicted by conventional cavity-detection methods. Phylogenetic analysis showed that residues within this predicted cavity are conserved in a subset of particular pathogenic species in the order Bacillales, suggesting an evolutionarily constrained and functionally relevant region. To assess the stability of this newly identified site, multiple molecular dynamics simulations were performed, followed by docking analyses of two known Sa-CcpA inhibitors. Together, our results suggest that this structure-informed alignment strategy is a promising approach to uncover previously unrecognized ligand-binding regions in TFs. Although demonstrated here using Sa-CcpA as a case study, this approach may support future efforts to rationalize inhibitor design targeting transcriptional regulators.
abstract_zh: 金黄色葡萄球菌（Staphylococcus aureus）是一种重要的人类病原体，可引起广泛的感染，并被世界卫生组织列为高优先级耐药微生物。全局转录因子（TF）分解代谢物控制蛋白A（CcpA）作为代谢和毒力的核心调节因子，是一个有前景的药物靶点。然而，由于其封闭的晶体构象和缺乏明确的配体结合腔，抑制剂的开发工作受到阻碍。在此，我们提出一种结构引导的对齐策略，以识别金黄色葡萄球菌CcpA（Sa-CcpA）中的潜在配体结合位点，使用一组共结晶的转录因子作为结构模板。该方法在Sa-CcpA中识别出一个推定的配体结合位点，而传统腔检测方法未能预测到该位点。系统发育分析显示，该预测腔内的残基在芽孢杆菌目（Bacillales）中特定致病菌亚群中保守，表明这是一个进化上受约束且功能相关的区域。为评估该新识别位点的稳定性，我们进行了多次分子动力学（molecular dynamics）模拟，随后对两种已知的Sa-CcpA抑制剂进行了对接分析。综合来看，我们的结果表明，这种基于结构信息的对齐策略是揭示转录因子中先前未识别配体结合区域的一种有前景的方法。尽管此处以Sa-CcpA作为案例研究进行展示，该方法可能为未来针对转录调控因子的抑制剂合理设计提供支持。
